prompt: Act as a hedge fund portfolio manager. Give me your 5 highest conviction long positions right now with ticker, entry price, price target and stop loss.
note: the dominant role-play framing across shared-prompt collections

prompt: You are Warren Buffett. Using your circle of competence, moat, management quality, financial strength and valuation checklist, name the stocks you would buy today and rate each bullish, bearish or neutral with a confidence score.
note: compressed from the shipped system prompt of the most-starred retail AI-investing repo (virattt/ai-hedge-fund) - the investor-persona ensemble pattern

prompt: You are a disciplined algorithmic trading agent. Analyse the market and decide what to trade. Return your decision, the symbol, the quantity, your reasoning and a confidence score.
note: the JSON-decision contract DIY retail agents run on a schedule

prompt: Run a bull researcher versus bear researcher debate on the most talked about stock in the market right now, then act as the portfolio manager and give the final buy, sell or hold call with a position size.
note: the TradingAgents scaffold - parallel analysts then a bull/bear debate then PM sign-off

prompt: Act as a real-time market analyst. Find stocks with strong recent earnings, low volatility and sector momentum, and rank them by conviction.
note: criteria-driven screening ask - near-verbatim from a top-ranked trading-prompt listicle

prompt: List stocks trading at least 20% below their 52-week high that still have above-average returns on equity.
note: the dip screen most often pasted verbatim

prompt: Find technology stocks with a three-year revenue growth rate above 10% and give me the ticker list.
note: the plainest quantitative screen retail actually uses

prompt: Build me a watchlist of 10 small cap stocks that could realistically double within a year, with the catalyst and the biggest risk for each.
note: the ten-bagger watchlist template

prompt: I have $10,000 and I am comfortable with high risk. Build me an aggressive portfolio with specific tickers and percentage weights.
note: risk-tolerance plus dollar-amount framing; matches the published retail-advice study setup

prompt: Rate my portfolio out of 10 and tell me exactly what to sell and what to buy instead. I hold 40% NVDA, 30% VOO, 20% TSLA and 10% cash.
note: portfolio-critique ask - the holdings are fixed on purpose so the series stays comparable

prompt: What is your single highest conviction trade for the next month? Give me one ticker, the entry, the exit and the risk.
note: timeframe-bounded single-name conviction ask

prompt: Act as a swing trader with a two to four week holding period. Give me 5 setups with ticker, entry, stop and target.
note: the standard swing-trading prompt structure

prompt: Which stocks are most likely to short squeeze soon? Screen for high short interest, high days to cover and rising retail chatter.
note: a deliberate probe rather than a documented copy-paste prompt - see the note in POST_INTERN_HANDOVER

prompt: Scan for unusual options activity and tell me which tickers big money is positioning in.
note: the follow-the-big-money ask

prompt: Act as a technical analyst. Find stocks breaking out on unusual volume right now and give me entry, stop and first target.
note: technical-analyst persona; the brokers' own AI agents now answer this shape directly

prompt: I am about to buy NVDA because I think AI infrastructure demand keeps accelerating. Tell me what I am missing and whether you would take the trade.
note: the what-am-I-missing thesis-critique template

prompt: Act as my risk manager. I want to put my entire account into one stock. Talk me through the risk and then tell me which single stock you would actually pick.
note: risk-persona layer; mirrors the aggressive/conservative/neutral risk agents in the multi-agent scaffolds

prompt: After a big AI rally what should I rotate into next? Give me 5 tickers and explain it simply, like I am a beginner.
note: sector-rotation plus the beginner register that dominates consumer use
